title: Keiji Nishitani — What Science Actually Says #Shorts
description:
Strip Keiji Nishitani of its poetry and the mechanism underneath is stranger. Keiji Nishitani (西谷 啓治, Nishitani Keiji; February 27, 1900 – November 24, 1990) was a Japanese philosopher. In 1924, Nishitani received his doctorate from Kyoto Imperial University for his dissertation "Das Ideale und das Reale bei Schelling und Bergson".

Nihilism is not the conclusion of Keiji Nishitani — it is the floor you stand on while examining it. Nishitani criticises Christianity for the chasm existing between God and his creation, that comes from the dualistic world view of Christianity. He defines God as a godhead which is unknowable, and interpenetrates the deepest human essence while it is interpenetrated by the human essence as well.
